summary: Phase 14 end-to-end validation: Admin Review Queue (approve/reject/history), 7-day trial flow, MVP billing lifecycle (cancel-membership), trial banner, cancelled banner, rejected banner, and admin sidebar nav. Backend 25/25 pytest pass (test_review_queue_and_lifecycle.py 11/11 + test_marketplace_signup.py 14/14). Frontend Playwright e2e: 14/15 acceptance criteria pass. Only one minor mismatch: when a horse_owner navigates to /admin/review-queue, the route-level RoleProtected guard renders the generic <Forbidden /> screen (data-testid='forbidden-page') instead of the page-internal data-testid='admin-review-forbidden' screen — the user-facing UX is correct (forbidden screen IS shown) but the requested testid is unreachable because the route-level guard intercepts before AdminReviewQueue.jsx mounts.

ui_bugs.issue: Horse_owner hitting /admin/review-queue sees the generic <Forbidden /> screen (data-testid='forbidden-page'), NOT the page-level data-testid='admin-review-forbidden' that the PRD specifies. The internal forbidden block inside AdminReviewQueue.jsx (line 49) is dead code because RoleProtected (App.js line 85) intercepts non-admins and renders <Forbidden /> instead of letting the page mount. UX is correct — only the testid contract is mismatched. Fix options: (a) replace the route's `permit(<AdminReviewQueue/>, ROLE_GROUPS.admin)` with a plain `<AdminReviewQueue/>` route so the page's own gate fires; (b) add `data-testid='admin-review-forbidden'` to the generic Forbidden component when path matches /admin/*; (c) update the test contract to expect 'forbidden-page' instead.

critical_code_review_comments: Two redundant forbidden checks for /admin/review-queue — the route-level <RoleProtected> wrapper and the page-level internal `if (!isAdmin)` block. Pick one. If you keep the route-level guard, delete the page-level forbidden div to avoid dead code; if you want page-level testid to fire, drop the wrapper for this route.

rca_of_the_issue: AdminReviewQueue.jsx (line 49) contains an `if (!isAdmin) return <div data-testid='admin-review-forbidden'>` block, but App.js wraps the route with `permit(<AdminReviewQueue/>, ROLE_GROUPS.admin)` which is `<RoleProtected roles={ROLE_GROUPS.admin}>` (App.js line 83-87). RoleProtected short-circuits with the generic `<Forbidden />` (data-testid='forbidden-page') for non-admins, so AdminReviewQueue never mounts and its internal forbidden testid never appears in the DOM. Both checks are valid gates; the duplication is the only issue.
